chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Hamzah ibn Ya'la, from al-Barqi, from Ubayd ibn al-Husayn, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

For your voluntary fasting, you may break the fast at any time before nightfall, whenever you wish; and for your making up the missed obligatory fast, you may break it until the sun sets, but once the sun has set, you may no longer break it.

key_terms.صَوْمُ قَضَاءِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: Making up the missed obligatory fast

ai.seo_question: When can I break my voluntary fast versus my make-up fast for Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic distinction between voluntary and obligatory fasts, noting that while nafl fasts allow breaking at any time before nightfall, qada fasts require maintaining the fast until sunset (ghurub al-shams). This ruling underscores the stricter binding nature of making up missed obligatory duties, reflecting the principle that qada approximates the original fard in its legal constraints.
